In response to [this](https://github.com/openshift/cluster-dns-operator/pull/482):

>## Summary
>- Vendor `openshift/api` to pick up `TLSProfileSpec.Groups` (`TLSGroupPreferences`) and bump `k8s.io` dependencies to v0.35.1
>- CoreDNS DaemonSet's kube-rbac-proxy sidecar now derives TLS cipher suites and minimum TLS version dynamically from the cluster-wide APIServer TLS security profile instead of hardcoded values
>- Operator watches the APIServer "cluster" resource and reconciles when the TLS policy changes
>- TLS curves/groups are not explicitly passed to kube-rbac-proxy (no `--tls-curves` flag); Go 1.25 `crypto/tls` defaults already include `X25519MLKEM768` (ML-KEM post-quantum) when `CurvePreferences` is unset
>
>## Jira
>https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/NE-2743
>
>## Test plan
>- [ ] Unit tests pass (`go test ./pkg/operator/controller/`)
>- [ ] Verify kube-rbac-proxy args are dynamically set from APIServer TLS profile
>- [ ] Verify reconciliation triggers on APIServer TLS profile change
>- [ ] Verify fallback to Intermediate profile when APIServer config is absent
>- [ ] e2e validation on cluster with DEFAULT:PQ crypto policy
>

`@Thealisyed`, my feedback is there — it was posted as **inline review comments on the "Files changed" tab** rather than as a single top-level comment, which is likely why it wasn't obvious. Here's a summary of the actionable items I flagged:

1. **`pkg/operator/controller/tls.go` (Lines 20‑32)** — `TLSProfileSpecForSecurityProfile` returns an empty `TLSProfileSpec` when `Type=Custom` and `Custom` is `nil`. This should fall back to the `Intermediate` profile from `configv1.TLSProfiles`, otherwise downstream code emits an invalid `--tls-min-version=` flag.

2. **`pkg/operator/controller/controller_dns_daemonset.go` (Lines 160‑177)** — `kubeRBACProxyArgs` has a fallback for empty `Ciphers` but not for `MinTLSVersion`. As defense-in-depth, add the same fallback there so this function is robust even if the caller passes a malformed profile.

3. **`pkg/operator/controller/tls_test.go` (Lines 62‑68)** — The "Custom profile with nil Custom field defaults to empty" test case doesn't assert `MinTLSVersion`, so it masks the bug above. Add an explicit `expectMinVer` assertion.

4. **`go.mod` (Line 58)** — `go.opentelemetry.io/otel` and `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/trace` are still pinned to v1.36.0, which is affected by `GHSA-mh2q-q3fh-2475` (CVE-2026-29181, a DoS via multi-value baggage header parsing). Please bump both to v1.41.0 or newer.

5. **Nitpick — `pkg/operator/controller/controller.go` (Lines 111‑118)** — The APIServer watch predicate only filters by object name, so any unrelated field change on `APIServer/cluster` triggers a DNS reconcile. Consider comparing `TLSSecurityProfile` between old/new objects to avoid unnecessary reconciliation.

`@Thealisyed` Yes, that all makes sense — I verified each point against the current code and my original comments don't hold up:

1. Confirmed — there's no `tls.go`; `tlsProfileSpecForProfile` and `kubeRBACProxyArgs` both live in `controller_dns_daemonset.go`, and the Custom/nil case already falls back to Intermediate.

Hi @Thealisyed so more of a top level comment here:
The approach here of plumbing the TLS profiles through to the kube-rbac-proxy sidecar is a lot of work for a component that is actually being phased out.

Upstream Kubernetes (sig-auth) has deprecated the gcr.io/kubebuilder/kube-rbac-proxy image due to security concerns, and it's no longer being published. Across OpenShift, there is a major ongoing migration (tracked under [OCPSTRAT-1835](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/OCPSTRAT-1835)) to completely remove kube-rbac-proxy sidecars from all components.

Instead of investing effort into dynamically configuring the deprecated proxy, we should lift out kube-rbac-proxy entirely. Since cluster-dns-operator is a controller-runtime based operator, we can replace the sidecar with native supporting code from controller-runtime.

Starting in v0.16.0 (and we are on v0.23.1), controller-runtime provides `filters.WithAuthenticationAndAuthorization`, which natively embeds authn/authz into the operator's metrics server using TokenReview and SubjectAccessReview.

It will be a bigger change but I think we should pivot this PR (or open a new one) to implement this migration for the operator.

### Implementation Steps
  
To adopt this pattern for the operator's metrics:

- Update main.go: Configure the metrics server to use the filter.
```go
import "sigs.k8s.io/controller-runtime/pkg/metrics/filters"
// ...
metricsOpts := metricsserver.Options{
  BindAddress:   ":8443", // Or your preferred port
  SecureServing: true,
  FilterProvider: filters.WithAuthenticationAndAuthorization,
}
```
- Remove the Sidecar: Drop the kube-rbac-proxy container from the dns-operator Deployment manifest (manifests/0000_70_dns-operator_02-deployment.yaml).
- Update RBAC: Ensure the metrics endpoint has the proper RBAC so the OpenShift Prometheus service account can scrape it via TokenReview/SubjectAccessReview.

### Examples
Several operators have already completed this migration. Here are a couple of excellent references you can use as a blueprint:
- kubernetes-nmstate: Upstream PR #1426 (https://github.com/nmstate/kubernetes-nmstate/pull/1426) / Downstream PR #718 (https://github.com/openshift/kubernetes-nmstate/pull/718)
- Operator Framework (operator-controller): PR #216 (https://github.com/openshift/operator-framework-operator-controller/pull/216)
